question: Can next-hour reconstructed fluid volume and documented setting be predicted across patients without any previous fluid data?
reference: Unchanged independent-reference V4 labels and eligibility; no reconstruction changes
split: Unchanged development five patient-grouped folds, seed 20261017; no new historical holdout evaluation
clock: At origin h, all histories use k<h; static baseline obeys existing admission availability proxy
allowed_inputs: their past observation masks and ages

models.training_patient_weighted_median: Constant per output; fitted on training patients only
models.static_time_hgb: Static baseline plus injury time; no physiology or infusion history
models.observation_only_hgb: Static/time plus physiology observation ages and counts, without numerical physiology
models.physiology_only_hgb: Static/time plus six summary statistics of ten physiology fields; absolute regression, no residual anchor
models.full_history_hgb: Matched absolute-regression HGB with all original source summaries; explicit comparator allowed to see fluid history
models.physiology_only_nm: Same NM-v1 training and architecture budget; all 18 infusion columns forced missing and all six anchors unknown before preprocessing, summaries and inference; no anchor guard; three fixed seeds, numerical outputs averaged

hgb.preprocessing: training-only 63 quantile cuts, median bins and missing indicators

nm.anchor: unknown for every output; computational fill 0 learned from entirely missing anchor columns, with known flags false; no patient-fluid state

selection: Fixed models and budgets, no outer early stopping or parameter selection; all variants reported, not an oracle best selection
endpoints: volume activity F1 from numerical predictions
exact-hour changes derived from the SAME absolute setting prediction
statistics: 2000 paired patient-cluster bootstrap replicates; exploratory pointwise 95% intervals; seed dispersion separate
learnability_interpretation: Evidence requires no-fluid models to improve over training-median and static/time references across held patients; numerical physiology increment assessed against observation-only control. Weak performance does not prove information-theoretic impossibility.
scope: Predictability of documented/reconstructed historical care, not an optimal clinical fluid prescription; no pump telemetry or clinical outcome claims
